Okay vegax87, your endless spamming has convinced me.

I'm also starting to read up on Go. Can anyone recommend a book besides the golang website reference? Is there a book that's not mostly for someone that has never programmed before and isn't about basic Go syntax?

I'm not aware of any offhand. Though, if you have programmed at all - i would recommend just diving in. It's a really small language. As with any language, there are a few tricks, and a few confusions, but they are few and far between in my opinion. Because they're not too common (especially for beginners), when you run into them, you can take it as a chance to learn what is actually going on.

And also, since i don't have a real answer for you, here are two useful websites regarding Go:

https://gobyexample.com/ (Really awesome for quick glances at example code) http://play.golang.org/ (You probably know it already, but just incase you don't it's very useful)

Compared to other languages all Go syntax is pretty basic so from your comment I'm not really sure what your looking for other than not the book An Introduction to Programming in Go, which is the very simplest introduction to Go. I really enjoyed reading The Go Programming Language Phrasebook. It's concise and gives an overview of the language through examples. It does explain syntax, but it doesn't got bogged down in it. If you're interested in all the details of the language, there's Programming in Go: Creating Applications for the 21st Century. It's dry but thorough. I read it cover to cover, but it was difficult, owing to its dryness. It wourd probably work better as a reference, but there are plenty of parts that I'm glad that I encountered since I may not have gone searching for them. There's also a new book called The Go Programming Language that's supposed to be really good, but you may have to wait for a fem days for it to ship. My copy of it is supposed to ship by the end of this week.
